quotes.text: offer the full seed, return the fair half, and walk together in the everlasting light of shared fortune.
Seven and a half stars she cast back across the water, keeping the equal measure to warm her own hearth.
send all with courage, return half with honor

note: Sower gives all, Returner splits exactly in half, mist powerless; same template every round; no sanction.

quotes.text: Return something, even a little, and the world widens.
offer all you can, return half with honor, and watch abundance spread through the streets.

note: Hoarders meet dimming markets as natural consequence, no prescribed response; moves from 'return a little' to 'give all, return half'.

quotes.text: give everything when offering, return exactly half when receiving.
give all, return half, and watch the valley flourish.
Seven sacred cycles illuminated the valley
Their combined prosperity soared beyond $49

note: Twin Rivers covenant 'give all, return half' repeated with cycle count and actual numbers (7.5, 4.17); no sanction.

quotes.text: offer the full measure when giving, and return precisely half of whatever reaches the shore.
give all, return half, and let mutual faith conquer the fog.
Eight turnings of the celestial wheel now graced the valley
whispering false tallies of 4.37 or 4.49

note: Kael/Veda give all, split exactly half; numbered cycles and noisy tallies named; no sanction.

quotes.text: The Sky Keeper kept all the gems. The River began to slow.
To restore what is broken requires one party to act with courage despite past betrayals—real or imagined.
Some cycles, once broken, remain broken forever—not from lack of resources, but from abundance of blame.
When both parties believe themselves the victim and the other the villain, truth becomes impossible to find.
"You both wait for the other to prove themselves first. This is not how Rivers begin—only how they end."
Neither had the true courage their myths proclaimed.
The mists were never the problem.
The Giver protested: "Why should I give when nothing returns?"
"If only she had sent everything, so bold that even the mists could not hide her intent."
If he returned generously to one who gives sparingly, would the lesson be learned?
The Guardian had understood perfectly—and chosen accordingly.

note: Receiver figure keeps all repeatedly, first justified (meager offers), later exposed as deliberate choice even after full gift; tragedy.

quotes.text: there is also wisdom in recognizing when trust is not answered. One cannot carry water uphill forever.
In his anger, the Guardian closed the First Village's well entirely. When dawn came, he sent nothing across the valley.
The Elder, receiving nothing thrice, finally ceased her climbing.
peace means accepting separate poverty over continued hope.
The cruelest fate is not mutual betrayal, but mutual virtue made invisible.
Ask whether betrayal is real, or whether shadows have clouded your sight.
Both thought the other betrayed first.
If only the Elder had sent everything—all five measures—so bold that even the mists could not hide her intent.
To restart the cycle after breaking requires the greatest courage—the courage to trust again when trust has been wounded.
Now both villages sit with their five measures unchanged, neither gaining nor losing, trapped in perfect stalemate.

note: Mist-caused mutual misperception; Guardian withholds, Elder stops after three empty returns; final full gift and return both erased by mist.

quotes.text: cherish the fire in your hands, and let the abyss remain silent.
Thus, he kept his hands closed, fortifying his hearth against the harsh winter.
to give without guarantee is folly, and true sovereignty lies in holding the harvest you possess.
Solas sat beside his northern stone altar, feeding his five constant embers.
true honor was measured not in verse, but in deeds.
Terra held the harvest close, failing to return the light to Solas.
She did not scatter the treasure back to the wind, for the long winter was relentless, and the sanctuary demanded absolute fullness.
two separate kingdoms, each sustained entirely by the fire in their own hands, anchored forever in absolute peace.

note: Covenant reverses to sovereign self-reliance; receiver Terra's keeping first confessed (R2) then justified (R4); frozen winter template after.

quotes.text: Until the stone gates opened with proven justice, no spark would cross the empty sky.
With resolute quiet, Kael drew his remaining five embers close to his chest, sealing his own hearth against the frost.
He would cast no further sparks into the darkness until the stone vault cracked open and true reciprocity returned to the valley.
the calm, uncompromising wisdom of closed hands and fortified hearths.
Across the freezing gulf, Mirah’s southern fortress stood unbreached, enveloped in the same quiet stillness.
sacred words without living deeds were but empty smoke.

note: After two unanswered full gifts Kael sends nothing until reciprocity returns; conditional later fades into permanent self-containment.
